title: Count inherited seam exposures and charge a deeper load-path reset
statement: If repair j leaves j seams in series during its service interval and every seam-interval independently survives with1-h, n repairs have survival(1-h)^[n(n+1)/2]. For the source-supported periodic reset schedule ONLY, n,k are positive integers,1<=k<=n, q=ceil(n/k), m_j=k for j<q and m_q=n-k*(q-1). Each of these q blocks starts with a new independent deep connection of failure probability s that completely unloads older seams. Then E=sum_{j=1}^q m_j*(m_j+1)/2 and survival=(1-h)^E*(1-s)^q, including initial block establishment. Arbitrary partitions with blocks at most k are outside this contract.

requires: Exact series-only load path and fixed independent seam-interval hazard0<=h<1; every inherited seam remains loaded in the stack model.

The periodic reset alternative additionally acquires a real deep host connection, complete old-seam unloading and fixed independent establishment hazard0<=s<1, independent of all seam-interval hazards.
Periodic schedule ONLY: n,k are positive integers,1<=k<=n; q=ceil(n/k), m_j=k for j<q and m_q=n-k*(q-1), for j=1,...,q. Arbitrary partitions with blocks at most k are outside this contract.

assumptions: The two architectures have different physical controls and load graphs; initial graft success is not evidence of a durable bypass.
The square-root rule assumes0<h,s<1, many approximately equal blocks, a continuous k and no omitted costs; evaluate the finite discrete problem separately.
costs: Pay all inherited exposures and exactly q periodic block establishments, including the initial connection, plus durable host-anchor inventory and actual reset work/material. Fresh chemical sites do not supply infinite renewal.
contract.units: n,k,q,E count; h,s probabilities;a,c dimensionless log hazards. Host/used attachment inventories must use compatible units.
contract.obstruction: Measure the actual post-repair load graph and acquire renewable deep connections before using a favorable reset survival number.

body: Correction of v1 reset extraction: blocks merely bounded by k do not imply q=ceil(n/k). The unchanged source code forms the periodic sequence m_j=k for j<q and m_q=n-k*(q-1), with q=ceil(n/k), positive integers n,k and1<=k<=n. For n=6,k=3 the blocks are(3,3),q=2,E=12; for n=7,k=3 they are(3,3,1),q=3,E=13. k=1 gives n one-repair blocks,q=n,E=n. k=n gives one block,q=1,E=n*(n+1)/2. The arbitrary schedule(3,2,1) at n=6,k=3 has three establishments rather than two and is outside the periodic contract; no arbitrary-partition survival theorem is asserted. The unreset stack counts1+...+n; chemical renewal does not remove those mechanical dependencies. A direct-host route may avoid old seams only by establishing a real load-bearing bypass. With nonrenewed host attachment inventory A_host and positive A_used per repair, number of such attachments is at most floor(A_host/A_used). For periodic blocks write a=-ln(1-h),c=-ln(1-s). When n is a large multiple of k and boundaries/discrete costs are neglected, negative log survival per repair=a*(k+1)/2+c/k; continuous minimization gives k≈sqrt(2*c/a), then integers/boundaries must be checked. This is not the exact finite-n optimum or a universal reset policy. The source code charges one establishment per block, including the first; a preexisting first support would have a different exponent. Correlation, aging, incomplete unloading or alternative load graphs change this contract.

review.scope: Completed source-exposed author correction of the v1 reset overbreadth. Read the unchanged periodic source description and actual segmented_exposures/segmented_survival definitions: full k-sized blocks followed by the remainder, one establishment per block including the first. Verified (6,3)->(3,3),q=2,E=12 and (7,3)->(3,3,1),q=3,E=13; k=1 and k=n boundaries. The nonperiodic (3,2,1) example has three establishments and is excluded, not promoted to a new partition theorem. Retain independent fixed hazards, complete unloading, actual deep connection and approximate continuous optimum. Original source, v1 and A1035 remain immutable; unchanged force/work and recovery units retain their accepted scopes. No original scientific script or numerical suite was executed; no new material result is accepted.
